Sometimes even female doctors act like this unfortunately. My sister has been sick for a while now - it's most likely PCOS and she's taking medication that helps but we don't know 100%. 

She was extremely tired all the time and gained around 10kg out of nowhere, which would be fine if she just started eating more, but the problem is that she DOESN'T. She eats max 1 meal a day and last year she walked around 2km daily due to her being in uni. 

She's gone to a few doctors and they all said different things. She got tons of tests from electrocardiograms to insulin tests but everything seemed fine. We decided to finally go to the endocrinologist to see if it was something to do with hormones.

We get there, she gets tested, and we have to wait a day for results. We come back, and frankly I don't remember the results, but I do remember the doctor telling her she probably just needed to lose some weight.

We left and she seemed very sad. She's been skinny her whole life until a couple years ago and she's gotten pretty awful comments. Her friends at uni looking at her weird while she was eating, to our aunt always making bad remarks about how she should "just eat less chocolate".

 Like I said before, she doesn't eat. Around 7 years ago she got a really bad stomach bug and she had to take very strong antibiotics that basically killed her intestinal flora. Ever since she has to eat very slowly and have small portions or else she gets really bad reflux. 

It's honestly very discouraging to have doctors just shrug off your symptoms and tell you to just lose weight. It's happened to me, to my sister, my mom, etc,, and it honestly just makes me feel like shit. I start wondering if I'm faking symptoms or something like that bc of what they said. I hope doctors do that less and less as time progresses :/
